kata.name: Mediator hub-exclusivity discovery question - underconstraint raises the shared-hub question on a one-hub model where it is vacuously true; a question is not a detection (null result)
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md mediator row (disposed; discovery-only candidate); fixtures/katas/mediator/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.5
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered null result: the hub-exclusivity question (listener;hub = speaker;hub) is raised verbatim as hypothesized, names no row, and is raised on a one-hub model where range forces the answer; empty unique = killed. The exclusivity-as-absence half (no direct colleague-to-colleague edge) has no surface at all

expected.detail: underconstraint raises parallel_paths listener;hub vs speaker;hub ('should these agree?') as hypothesized, together with listener vs speaker. Both are schema-level questions: no row, no truth value, and the shared-hub question is vacuous on a one-hub model because every hub cell can only be hub_main

the pattern's stronger claim is that no colleague-to-colleague edge exists. The schema has no such arrow and the kernel has no negative-arrow or universal form, so the claim is unexpressible; exclusivity survives only as the positive equation-shaped question above

commands: python3 prototype/mediator_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: baseline reports no detection; the discovery arm is exercised
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/mediator/mediator.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- underconstraint fixtures/katas/mediator/mediator.ct.json --max-path-length 2 --json  # exit 6, 2 hypothesized findings

comparison.conventional_baseline: the frozen per-arrow suite asserts every cell resolves and every documented route matches; the clean one-hub model passes, and the suite raises no discovery question.

baseline.artifact: prototype/mediator_baseline.py sha256:863b8c04a045b7571242b172540e0ba172aece8df9071ba37dd0263460b456d3 (frozen per-arrow suite: hub/party/dispatch range assertions plus the documented-route table; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: both participants of one interaction share one hub, as an accepted equation
expressibility_gap.why: the pair is not related by a declared equation; the kernel raises it only as a hypothesized parallel-path question (direct-only relating, crates/catherine-analysis/src/parallel.rs). A question has no witness row and no verdict, so it cannot be promoted to a survived claim. Accepting it as an equation was out of this kata's pre-registered scope

absence of an arrow is schema structure; equations relate declared paths and there is no universal/existential or negative-arrow form. The kernel cannot state or check the prohibition, so it is a named gap

discrepancies: The exclusivity question is raised even though a single Mediator row forces both sides of it, so the discovery surface is schema-level and instance-blind: it cannot distinguish a real second-center risk from a vacuous question. Recorded as a question, never counted as a detection.

The disposition row's candidate ('discovery questions over hub exclusivity/coherence') is half validated: coherence is a law with a truth value (entries 2 and 3, scoped), exclusivity is a question (this entry, killed), and absence is a gap.
procedure: 1. The law was named before any fixture was written (README: dispatch coherence `dispatched_by = participant ; hub`; exclusivity and absence named as the discovery-only and inexpressible halves). The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/mediator/ (README.md, faults.json) before the recorded run; nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/mediator_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: per-arrow assertions over every row (colleague hub declared; interaction parties declared and distinct; dispatch declared; documented route matched). It never composes two arrows and never asserts a specific mediator row.
3. The probe arm ran the same fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json`, plus `catherine underconstraint --max-path-length 2 --json` where the discovery question belongs to the entry.

4. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements (<object>:<name>); unique_detections = executed probe elements minus baseline-identified elements. Hypothesized underconstraint findings are questions, recorded verbatim and never counted as detections.
5. Verdict follows the recorded rule: empty unique = killed; non-empty unique with an executed baseline arm = survived.
